data.summary: I built a distinct-root-cause ledger for each PR from the code (not the other dimensions' write-ups), verified each defect's mechanism and fix size, and resolved the contradictions that touch deduplication. PR 9 has one dominant root cause (an argv/permission/blocked-handling family at md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220 and automatic.py:207-208) whose code fix is three source lines plus one test, but whose real cause is the skipped merge-gating live smoke test; PR 10 has one dominant root cause (EXPORT_VERSION 1.2.0 vs main's z.literal('1.0.0')) whose fix is one line, but its blast radius is larger than PR 10's handoff admits because `workflow.pipeline <run> status` calls report() which re-exports the live run (pipeline.py:688). PR 11's dominant issue (implementing B and C directly) is not a code defect and has no fix; its remaining distinct defects are all low. Charged once each, the three PRs land within 1.5 points of each other: PR 11 7.0, PR 10 6.5, PR 9 5.5. Deduplication removes roughly six duplicate charges from PR 9, about ten from PR 10 and about six from PR 11, which shifts per-dimension averages by well under 1 point and does not move any PR by 2 or more, so the ranking PR 11 > PR 10 > PR 9 on quality survives, with the gap between PR 10 and PR 11 narrowing to a coin flip that depends on how much weight the PRD's shipping plan gets.
data.pr9: Distinct defects (charged once each): (1) HIGH, launch family: `--add-dir <dir>` is variadic per `claude --help` line 10 ("--add-dir <directories...>"), so md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:220 `"--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]` hands the prompt to --add-dir and the session starts idle; no `--allowedTools` so under dontAsk the single Write is denied (PR 10 and PR 11 both saw this live); automatic.py:207-208 then treats native `blocked` as fatal. Fix is ~3 source lines (reorder so the prompt follows `--permission-mode`, add `--allowedTools f"Edit(//{run}/review.completion.json)"`, replace the raise with a note-and-keep-polling) plus rewriting the second half of test_automatic.py:255-260 and the HANDOFF/VALIDATION sentences that describe the old argv. The root cause is not the code but the skipped gate: PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md line 60 says the controlled live smoke test runs "before merging", and the handoff line 63 admits it was not run and even predicts the exact fallback at line 55. (2) MEDIUM, status() at interactive.py:242-249 iterates NODES only and attach_panels (295-338) only ever maps ui/adapter, while PRD item 3 (line 53) asks for "third pane in attach_panels and attach-one"; the reviewer is reachable only through attach_reviewer_pane/attach-one. Fix ~3 lines (PR 11 shows the shape at md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:232). (3) LOW, kept a hand copy of the print-mode REVIEW_SCHEMA (automatic.py:133-141) beside the generated JSON instead of deriving it as PR 10 does; this copy is inherited from main automatic.py:116 and PR 11 keeps it too, so it is charged equally to both. (4) NIT, two names for one node: REVIEWER="reviewer" (sessions.py:20), file_prefix maps to "review" (sessions.py:24-26), receipt node_id "review", `attach-one --node reviewer`; internally consistent but a trap for operators reading PR 10/11 docs. Strengths: smallest and PRD-conformant scope, zod-first contract with generated schema and contract tests (contracts diff +174 across v1.ts/examples/contract.test.ts/schema), honest handoff. Score 5.5: one severe functional defect charged once, but the feature has never run live and the merge gate is unmet, so unknown unknowns remain even after the 3-line fix.
data.pr10: Distinct defects: (1) HIGH, md-manager-high/workflow/export_state.py:16 `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"` while main server/projects.ts:37/52 validates `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)` with '1.0.0'. Blast radius verified: main listRuns (server/projects.ts:320-345) calls projectRun inside try/finally with no catch, so one invalid run-state throws invalidRun for the whole workflow list; and `python -m workflow.pipeline <run> status` calls `report(runtime, state)` (md-manager-high/workflow/pipeline.py:688, same as main pipeline.py:600) which calls export_state, so a plain `status` on project-workflows-001 after merge rewrites its run-state.json to 1.2.0 and hides the workflow. The handoff (line 76-78) discloses the new-run window and warns only against `workflow export`, not `status`, so the disclosure is incomplete. Fix is one line either side: `version: z.enum(['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0'])` at server/projects.ts:52 (main exportSchema is z.object, zod ^4.6.5, so the extra `review`/`inputs` keys are stripped, not rejected) plus one server test; or keep `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.0.0"` in export_state.py. (2) MEDIUM, the completion binds `reviewer_session` and the prompt (automatic.py:159) tells the reviewer to use "your own session UUID as shown by `claude agents`", but the reviewer has tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write only and cannot run it. The smoke transcript (~/.claude/projects/-home-agentops--local-state-md-manager-workflows-smoke-review-smoke-001-review-worktree/5865c9a6-....jsonl) shows the UUID first enters the model's context at record 204 (Grep result on events.jsonl) and 299 (Read of automatic-review.json), and its first assistant use is the Write at record 310; no earlier assistant mention exists. So the binding works only because the controller leaks the UUID into readable run-dir files; a reviewer that does not go hunting fails the whole review with "no second reviewer". Fix: one prompt line naming review.interactive.json, or ~15 lines to bind a pre-launch token as PR 9/11 do. (3) LOW-MEDIUM, wait_review's stop-recovery branch (automatic.py:196-198) is unreachable from review_candidate: a "running" receipt goes review_native -> run_reviewer -> reconcile (interactive.py:117-128) which raises when locate() finds no live row, and locate (interactive.py:82) only accepts idle/working/blocked/done. So the post-acceptance crash window (stop.json written, receipt still "running") is unhandled and test_stopped_reviewer_recovery_rereads_the_accepted_file (test_automatic.py:572-576) exercises dead code. PR 11 handles this window at md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:236-241. (4) LOW, contracts/projects/v1.ts:127-133 requires `reviewer_transport` in `automatic` while export_state.py:103 copies `plan.get("automatic")` verbatim (absent for project-workflows-001); the adapter task (features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md:11) and README:46 tell the adapter worker to default it to "print". The contract describes the API response, not the file, and the mapping is documented, so LOW, not HIGH. (5) MEDIUM scope, bundles B/C contracts, export and feature dirs into A's PR against PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY's "ship A alone"; but it stops at the pre-run work, which is what the PRD says precedes each feature run. Strengths: structured_review_schema() (automatic.py:134-138) derives the print schema from the completion schema (single source); reconcile() covers the launch-window interruption in 12 lines; two live smoke runs with cost and transcript recorded. Score 6.5.
data.pr11: Distinct defects: (1) HIGH (process, not code), all three slices implemented directly in a 56-file, +6074/-333 commit, against the umbrella PRD's explicit plan (PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md lines 18-19: B and C ship as feature runs, "each run has a smaller, focused diff") and against the point of the product, which is to run such work as feature runs. Disclosed in the handoff line 3. This is charged in 2 dimensions and rewarded in 3 (adapter 8.5, UI 8, export-and-compat credit); on a dedup view the penalty belongs in spec-fidelity and reviewability only, and the delivered code is legitimately scored where it is. It has no fix: it can only be accepted or the PR reduced to its slice-A subset (pr11-sliceA.diff, 14 files, +1699/-178). (2) LOW-MEDIUM, contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json is hand-written (39 lines, no v1.ts/examples/contract.test.ts entry; `git diff 61e4752 --stat -- contracts/` shows only README +2 and the schema +39 under contracts/workflow). It is comparable in strictness to PR 9's generated one (same required set, additionalProperties false on both levels, patterns on every id) and the README addition says "hand-written, not generated from v1.ts", so the convention break is disclosed; only the handoff's blanket line 48 ("npm run contracts:export regenerated the JSON schemas") overstates it. Charge once, LOW-MEDIUM; fix ~60 lines. (3) LOW, features/review-result and features/run-inputs ship READMEs that say "the committed assignment for the two workers ... not an implementation" while the implementation is in the same tree; launching them would assign already-done work. Disclosed (handoff line 3, line 77). Fix: delete or rewrite. (4) LOW, same inherited hand copy of REVIEW_SCHEMA (automatic.py:129-141) as PR 9. Not charged: `_decide` rewriting approved-with-open-P1 to blocked (automatic.py:277-289) keeps the raw decision in `receipt["decision"]` and is documented (handoff line 69), so it is a design choice, not lossy; the launch_token binding instead of the session UUID is the stronger design given what the PR 10 transcript shows. Strengths: the two live-discovered CLI facts are documented at the point of use (interactive.py:215-223 comments), status() includes the reviewer, the adapter accepts 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 (server/projects.ts:44,145) so the live run keeps loading, the post-acceptance stop is retried (automatic.py:236-241), the prompt enumerates every allowed value after attempt 3's "P3" (automatic.py:172-174), and the export records the transport actually used (export_state.py:148). Score 7.0.
data.ranking_reason: With each root cause charged exactly once, PR 11 has one high issue that is procedural (scope), three lows, and no verified functional defect; PR 10 has one high functional trap (a one-line fix, but its `status`-rewrites-the-live-run path is undisclosed), one medium design flaw the transcript confirms, and three lows; PR 9 has one high functional defect (a three-line fix, but the feature has never run and the PRD's merge gate is unmet), one medium, and two nits. The gaps are narrow (7.0 / 6.5 / 5.5). Dedup narrows PR 9's and PR 10's distance to PR 11 by roughly 0.5-0.8 on a per-dimension average but does not move any PR by 2 or more, so the quality ranking holds; it would flip PR 10 above PR 11 only if the person weights adherence to the PRD's shipping plan more than the umbrella-level tradeoff of a 6k-line single commit.

findings.title: PR 9's launch failure is one root cause charged in seven dimensions; the code fix is three lines, the real cause is the skipped merge gate
findings.detail: The variadic --add-dir swallowing the prompt, the missing --allowedTools rule and blocked-is-fatal are three symptoms of one decision: shipping the native launch without the live smoke test that PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md section 5 makes a merge gate. After that the person still has to run the gate PR 10 and PR 11 ran, because PR 9's code has never met a real session.

findings.detail: Charged once, EXPORT_VERSION 1.2.0 vs main's z.literal('1.0.0') is one HIGH with a one-line fix. Its blast radius is larger than PR 10 states: `python -m workflow.pipeline <run> status` calls report(), which calls export_state, so an operator running `status` on project-workflows-001 after merge rewrites run-state.json to 1.2.0; main's listRuns throws invalidRun with no per-run catch, so the whole workflow list 500s. findings.title: reviewer_session binding works only by file leakage; transcript settles the contradiction in favour of launch-attach-stop
findings.detail: The prompt tells the reviewer to report its UUID 'as shown by `claude agents`', but the reviewer has no Bash. In the live run the UUID entered the model's context only through a Grep on events.jsonl (record 204) and a Read of automatic-review.json (record 299); there is no earlier assistant mention, so 'the model's self-knowledge carried it' (spec-fidelity) is wrong. A reviewer that does not go looking fails the whole review, and the protocol never launches a second one. Fix: one prompt line naming review.interactive.json, or ~15 lines to bind a pre-launch token as PR 9/11 do.

findings.title: wait_review's stop-recovery branch is dead and the post-acceptance crash window is unhandled; the praised test exercises dead code
findings.detail: Resume with a 'running' receipt goes review_native -> run_reviewer -> reconcile, which raises when the stopped session is not in the inventory, so the `stop.exists()` branch in wait_review never runs in production.
